title: Every Knee, Every Tongue
hook: If God wants everyone saved, is He strong and wise enough to actually do it?
tldr: Scripture says God wants all people saved and that every knee will bow and every tongue confess. If God is all-powerful, all-wise and all-loving, anything short of total reconciliation means His will was thwarted. The bowing is not humiliation but freely chosen worship, as all creation falls in love with God.
big_idea: An all-powerful, loving God must finally win every heart, not just most.

points.title: God wants all saved
points.text: In every translation, 1 Timothy 2:4 says God wants or desires all people to be saved. The debate is not over His will but whether He is wise and powerful enough to accomplish it.

points.title: Only 10:0 is victory
points.text: If God and Satan compete for ten people, an all-powerful God cannot settle for 6:4 or 8:2. Saving 1% or 99% would mean He could be wiser and stronger than He is.

points.title: The trilemma of eternal loss
points.text: If anyone is eternally condemned, God is limited in power (unable to save all), wisdom (cannot convince all) or goodness (does not truly care to save all).

points.title: Bowing is freely chosen worship
points.text: Bowing the knee was honor reserved for gods and kings. Every knee bowing signifies freely chosen worship rooted in love, not fear, as all creation is won by divine persuasion.

points.title: Tongues swear loyal allegiance
points.text: In Isaiah 45:23 the tongue 'shall swear', a pledge of allegiance born of admiration, like subjects pledging their lives to their king. It is adoration, not humiliation.

points.title: Punishment corrects and refines
points.text: People may face consequences, penalties and lost rewards, but God's punishment is corrective, not destructive. Hell is best seen as a refining fire that purifies, preparing souls for reunion.

sections.summary: Humanity can seem like pawns in a cosmic struggle between God and Satan for human allegiance. Given God's omnipotence and omniscience, His will is destined to prevail. People may face consequences and corrective punishment, but the vast majority suffering eternal torment is hard to reconcile with the God of Israel, 'mighty to save' (Zephaniah 3:17). It would mean He cannot achieve His ultimate will that all be saved.

Free will is core to the divine-human relationship; God does not coerce love but shows His trustworthiness and goodness, since true love must prove itself. The Serpent's deception in Eden (Genesis 3:1) cast doubt on God's trustworthiness, so the cosmic battle is about human perception: whom will humans finally bow before, God or the Serpent? If God and Satan compete for ten people, the only acceptable result for an all-powerful God is 10:0, not 6:4 or 8:2.

sections.h: Is Yahweh really the strongest and wisest?
sections.summary: A short life gives only a glimpse of this cosmic war. Now we see dimly, but one day we will see face-to-face (1 Corinthians 13:12) and the earth will be filled with knowledge of the Lord's glory (Habakkuk 2:14). God does whatever pleases Him (Psalm 115:3); nothing is too hard for Him (Genesis 18:14; Jeremiah 32:17); His word is never powerless (Isaiah 55:11). He knows everything, the cosmic Grandmaster, including future events.

In Old Testament days God invited Israel to test Him and see His power, wisdom and goodness (Malachi 3:10; Isaiah 7:11; Isaiah 43:10). We finite creatures can examine whether He is the pinnacle of wisdom, power, love and goodness; if so, we can trust Him, reversing Genesis 3. Being strongest and wisest, His power and knowledge are limitless, and He can bring about any outcome without compromising anyone's free will. That is part of what makes Him God.

sections.h: Can God bring His will to fruition?
sections.summary: God's will is clear: He 'wants all people to be saved' (1 Timothy 2:4). Paul took this literally: at Jesus' name every knee should bow, in heaven, on earth and under the earth (Philippians 2:10), not a few, not most, but every knee. The NIV, NLV, ESV and KJV all agree God wants or desires everyone saved. Even without the Bible, a good and loving God would. The only question is whether He is wise and powerful enough.

sections.h: The Calvinist dilemma and John Piper
sections.summary: If God is omniscient, omnipotent and omnibenevolent and wills all to be saved, complete reconciliation of all souls, through their own free will, becomes a necessity. Augustinian-Calvinists must admit something stronger than God's will. John Piper says God wills all to be saved yet in another sense does not, some other will taking precedence. But the Bible is clear God wants all saved; the only questions are how and when, the day of unity under Christ (Ephesians 1:10).

Any outcome short of total reconciliation, saving 1% or even 99%, suggests God could be wiser and stronger. If He saved only a few, He would seem an impotent god, and we might look for stronger deities. If anything, free will, human stupidity, Satan or society, could negate His will by one inch, He would not be supreme. Deductively: God is supremely wise, powerful and loving; He wills all saved; so His will must come to fruition.

The modern Western Church sees salvation individualistically, reflecting cultural egocentrism, unlike the collective mindset of ancient societies, especially the Jewish people, where salvation was a communal endeavor benefiting the whole group. Eternal condemnation of anyone would limit God's power, wisdom or goodness. Total salvation is not naive hope but a litmus test for a consistent view of God. If God wills all to know Christ (1 Timothy 2:3-6), His power will achieve it, though we cannot know how or when.

Satan tries to convince humanity God cannot be trusted, but his power to deceive is temporary and inferior. 'As surely as I live... every knee will bow before me' (Romans 14:11) ties the promise to God's eternal life. Satan fights over souls, not land, distorting God's love into a self-centered, transactional, conditional, fear-based version. Yet God's plan rests on His unconditional, eternal nature; we live by faith until God restores everything (Acts 3:21).

Romans 14:11 points to a future where God's supremacy is universally recognized, His power to save outmatching Satan's deception. It repeats what God promised through the prophets: 'Before me every knee will bow; by me every tongue will swear' (Isaiah 45:23). Paul and Isaiah picture not few, not some, not many, but every knee and tongue acknowledging that Jesus Christ is Lord. But what does that submission mean?

In the ancient world, bowing the knees showed profound respect and allegiance, reserved for gods and kings. In Daniel 3:16-18, three Jewish men refuse to bow to King Nebuchadnezzar, keeping that honor for God alone. To the Hebrew mind, 'every knee will bow' means a freely chosen act of worship. True worship expresses love and respect, not fear (1 John 4:18).

The Hebrew word in Isaiah 45:23, tishaba, means 'shall take an oath' or 'to swear'. Subjects swore allegiance to a king going to war, even pledging their lives, out of admiration. So bowing and swearing mean surrender out of adoration, not humiliation, punishment or degradation. Simply put, all mankind will fall in love with God, shown in words and actions, as creation willingly, through divine persuasion, accepts Christ's lordship.

God is 'the mighty one who saves' (Zephaniah 3:17). He loves the world (John 3:16). His love means He wants all saved (1 Timothy 2:3). His 'love never fails' (1 Corinthians 13:8). His will always comes to fruition: 'No purpose of yours can be thwarted' (Job 42:2), and He 'works all things according to the counsel of his will' (Ephesians 1:11). Conclusion: every knee will bow and every tongue confess.

sections.h: What victory would the cross be?
sections.summary: If only a few are saved, what was Christ's death for? If His sacrifice beat death and hell yet hell prevails, redeeming a minority, death has the final word and the cross was mostly futile. Anything less than total victory fails the definition of an omnibenevolent, omnipotent, omniscient God. Condemning limited, emotional creatures to eternal torment for misunderstanding, fear or anger fits a pagan deity, not the Father revealed by Jesus.

As an Ashkenazi Jew, aware of his people's long history of abuse and attempted extermination, the writer admits longing for justice and even revenge. But God's will transcends human vengeance: He wants all to come, even the worst sinners. Leading even perpetrators of heinous acts to repent and believe would show Him the greatest, wisest, most loving being. God will reconcile all things through the blood of the cross (Colossians 1:20); Satan's victories are temporary.

Consequences, penalties and lost rewards remain, but they are corrective, not destructive. Life is divine transformation for rehabilitation and growth, not retribution. God is a loving Father, not a sadistic psychopath; good parents do not abuse children for ignorance or stubbornness. Punishment cleanses souls for reunion; Jesus atoned for the whole world's sins (1 John 2:1-2). Hell is a refining fire, and all the ends of the earth will turn to the Lord (Psalm 22:27).

The tongue's action in Isaiah 45:23: swearing loyal allegiance out of admiration, as subjects pledged their lives to a king.

mythfact.myth: Every knee bowing means the damned are forced into humiliated submission before being punished.
mythfact.fact: Bowing and swearing signify surrender out of adoration and respect. All mankind will fall in love with God, shown in words and actions.

mythfact.myth: God saving most people would still be a great victory.
mythfact.fact: Saving 1% or 99% would mean God could be wiser and stronger. For an all-powerful God, only 10:0 is acceptable.

mythfact.myth: Salvation is mainly an individual matter.
mythfact.fact: This reflects modern Western individualism. Ancient societies, especially the Jewish people, understood salvation as a communal endeavor benefiting the whole group.

mythfact.myth: God's punishment is endless suffering for its own sake.
mythfact.fact: It is corrective, not destructive: a refining fire that cleanses souls of the flaws that estranged them, preparing them for reunion.

quiz.q: In the ten-person thought experiment, what outcome fits an all-powerful God?
quiz.why: For God to fully triumph, He must win every single heart, matching every tongue confessing.

quiz.q: What does the Hebrew tishaba in Isaiah 45:23 mean?
options: Shall take an oath or swear
quiz.why: It is swearing allegiance out of admiration, like subjects pledging loyalty to their king.

quiz.q: If anyone stays eternally condemned, which attribute would be limited?
quiz.why: God would be unable to save all, unable to convince all, or not truly caring to save all.

reflect: Could you hope for the salvation of someone who deeply wronged you, as the writer does for his people's persecutors?
